folder.description: The folder to which the logging bucket configuration applies.
folder.rationale: Folder selection ensures the logging bucket is applied to the correct organizational hierarchy and impacts access controls and resource management.
folder.compliant: Proper folder ID with appropriate access controls and organizational alignment

location.description: The location of the logging bucket. This determines where log data is stored and impacts data residency requirements.
location.rationale: Location selection impacts data residency, compliance with regional regulations, and latency for log access and analysis.
location.compliant: Regions that comply with data residency requirements (e.g., australia-southeast1)
location.non-compliant: Unapproved or restricted regions that violate data residency policies

bucket_id.description: The ID of the logging bucket. This must be unique within the folder and location.
bucket_id.rationale: Bucket ID naming conventions help identify purpose, ownership, and classification of log data for proper security management.
bucket_id.compliant: Descriptive names following organizational naming conventions (e.g., security-logs, audit-trails, application-logs)
bucket_id.non-compliant: Generic or unclear names that don't indicate content or purpose

description.description: A description of the logging bucket's purpose and contents.
description.rationale: Clear descriptions help ensure proper classification, retention, and access controls for sensitive log data within the folder hierarchy.
description.compliant: Detailed description of bucket contents, purpose, and folder context
description.non-compliant: Missing or vague descriptions that don't clarify content sensitivity or purpose

retention_days.description: The number of days to retain log entries in this bucket. Setting this to null will use the default retention period.
retention_days.rationale: Proper retention periods ensure compliance with regulatory requirements while preventing unnecessary long-term storage of sensitive data at the folder level.
retention_days.compliant: Retention periods that meet regulatory requirements (e.g., 365 days for compliance, 30 days for operational logs)
retention_days.non-compliant: Inadequate retention periods that violate compliance requirements or excessive retention increasing attack surface

index_configs.description: Configuration for custom indexes on log fields to enable faster searching and analysis within the folder's log data.
index_configs.rationale: Index configuration impacts query performance and should be carefully managed to avoid indexing sensitive data unnecessarily within the folder context.
index_configs.compliant: Selective indexing of non-sensitive fields for operational monitoring and troubleshooting
index_configs.non-compliant: Indexing sensitive PII, security-related fields, or confidential business data that could expose information

field_path.description: Note that some paths are automatically indexed, and other paths are not eligible for indexing. See [indexing documentation](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/analyze/custom-index) for details.
field_path.rationale: Field path selection for indexing should avoid sensitive data to prevent exposure through search queries within the folder's log data.
field_path.compliant: Non-sensitive operational fields (e.g., severity, timestamp, resource.type, httpRequest.status)
field_path.non-compliant: Sensitive fields containing PII, credentials, security tokens, or business-confidential information

type.description: The type of index to create for the field path. Possible values include STRING, INTEGER, etc.
type.rationale: Index type selection should align with the data type and intended query patterns while considering security implications for folder-level log analysis.
type.compliant: Appropriate index type matching the field data type and query requirements
type.non-compliant: Mismatched index types that could impact performance, cost, or security monitoring capabilities
